user_prompt: What is the effect of diclofenac (any route: rectal, intravenous, intramuscular, oral; given before, during or after surgery) compared with an opioid analgesic (e.g. morphine, fentanyl, sufentanil, pethidine/meperidine, papaveretum, nalbuphine; any route including caudal/epidural) on the number of children who required rescue analgesic medication after surgery, in children aged under 18 undergoing any surgical procedure under general anaesthesia?  Effect measure: pool as a risk ratio (RR) using a random-effects model. RR < 1 means fewer children needing rescue analgesia in the diclofenac arm (favours diclofenac).  Outcome: number of children (events) and number randomised/analysed (total) in each arm who received any rescue or supplementary analgesic after surgery (also described as "analgesic complementation", "supplementary analgesia", "postoperative analgesia given", or "number requiring [opioid/paracetamol] postoperatively"), within the first 24 hours after surgery. - Use the count covering the longest postoperative window available up to 24 hours (e.g. recovery ward stay, first 4 hours, until discharge, 24 hours). Do not use a count limited to the first 2 hours when a longer window is also reported. - If the numbers are only given as percentages, convert them to counts using the group size. If they appear only in a figure or bar chart, read the percentage for each group from the figure and convert it to counts; do not exclude the study for that reason. - Multi-arm trials: use the diclofenac arm as the treatment group. Combine all opioid arms into one control group (sum events and totals). Ignore no-analgesia/placebo arms, local anaesthetic arms (e.g. caudal bupivacaine alone), paracetamol arms and other NSAID arms. - Extract from each study the single dichotomous rescue-analgesia count. Do not substitute time to first rescue analgesia, rescue dose consumed, or pain scores.  Do not pool pain intensity scores, time to rescue medication, opioid consumption, nausea/vomiting, bleeding or other adverse events. Exclude comparisons of diclofenac against placebo, paracetamol, other NSAIDs or local anaesthetics, and exclude studies in adults.
